memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect or flaw in it, for that would be detestable to him. - Deut 17:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins this chapter with a plain instruction, do not bring Him an animal that is blemished or flawed. A crippled or diseased animal cost the giver very little. To offer such a thing was really to say, "God can have whatever I no longer want." And God calls that attitude detestable.

This was never about God needing perfect livestock. It was about the heart behind the gift. God saw straight through the offering to the affection, or lack of it, that lay underneath. A careless sacrifice revealed a careless heart.

We should let this search us gently. We too can be tempted to give God our leftovers, the tired end of our energy, the spare minutes, the money we would not miss anyway. God is not honoured by grudging scraps. He gave His very best for us, His own Son, who was the unblemished Lamb, without spot or defect (1 Pet 1:19). At the cross, Christ offered Himself perfectly on our behalf, so we no longer bring animals at all. But the principle of the heart remains. Out of gratitude for His flawless gift, we offer Him our best, not our leftovers. Where might God be asking for your first and finest, rather than what is left over?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you tend to give God your leftovers?
2. What does your giving reveal about your heart toward Him?
3. How does Christ's perfect offering reshape the way you give?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for giving me Your very best in Jesus. Forgive my leftover offerings and teach me to give You my finest. Amen.
